title: Attacker price sheet fetched 2026-10-25: residential proxy, CAPTCHA, browser, LLM, VPS
summary: Residential proxy is billed per GB, not per IP-hour: Decodo PAYG $4/GB, 100GB $2.75, 1TB $2.00; Bright Data PAYG $4 (promo, list $8), $3/GB at $999/mo; Oxylabs $6/GB<=5GB ... $2.5/GB at 1TB+. Turnstile solve $1.45/1k (2Captcha), reCAPTCHA v2 $1-2.99/1k. Browserless unit=30 s, overage $0.0015-0.0020 => $0.18-0.24 per browser-hour. Zyte HTTP tier1 $0.06-0.13/1k, browser tier1 $0.48-1.01/1k; Bright Data Web Unlocker $1.30-1.50/1k. Claude API per MTok in/out: Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50, Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, Opus 5.5 $4/$20. VPS: DigitalOcean $4 1vCPU/512MiB/500GiB, $6 1vCPU/1GiB/1000GiB; Hetzner shared from EUR5.99 (shown 'currently not available'), EUR6.49. ISP static proxies ~$0.225-0.30/IP/mo (Webshare) to ~$2.40 (IPRoyal) per secondary sources.
specifics: All fetched 2026-10-25 from vendor pages. CapSolver pricing page 404; its $0.8-1.2/1k Turnstile figure is secondary (D). No provider prices per IP-hour for residential: 'IP-hour' must be derived from GB. ISP-proxy per-IP prices are affiliate-site secondary (D). OpenAI price page returned 403 (not used). Hetzner official CX23 price not confirmable (sources conflict EUR3.49-3.99).
overclaim_risk: Promo/volume pricing moves monthly; Bright Data $4 is a 50% promo of a $8 list.
underclaim_risk: Prices are floor-ish list prices; real operators on gray-market SDK pools (IPIDEA-class) pay far less than Decodo list, so these are conservative (high) attacker costs.

title: Attacker cost per 1M requests by attack class (derived from the price sheet)
summary: Using bytes/request (TLS full handshake 6 KB assumed, +2.26 KB hybrid ML-KEM) and $2/$4/$6 per GB: scrape (100 KB page) $286/$500/$713 per 1M if all admitted, $87/$101/$116 if all rejected; credential stuffing (10.5 KB, Turnstile solved per attempt) ~$1,470-1,513 per 1M of which $1,450 is CAPTCHA; expensive-endpoint (57 KB) $114/$228/$342 admitted, $15/$30/$44 rejected; MCP tool-spam scripted over keep-alive (4.6 KB) $9/$18/$28. Managed alternatives per 1M pages: Zyte HTTP $60-130 (tier1)..$610-1,270 (tier5), Zyte browser $480-16,080, Bright Data Unlocker $1,300-1,500, own Browserless at 4 s/page $200-267. LLM-driven agent steps dominate any scripted cost: per 1M MCP tool steps (1.5k in/250 out) Haiku 5.5 $275, Sonnet 5.5 $5,500, Opus 5.5 $11,000; browse step with screenshot (6k/400) $800 / $16,000 / $32,000. A rejected 429 still costs the attacker its TLS handshake bytes (7.4 KB), so rejects are not free for the attacker either: ~$30 per 1M on mid proxies.
specifics: Sheet: 07-work/cost_model.json (script cost_model.py). Byte sizes are assumptions (E) except the ML-KEM delta (Red Sift measured +1,088 B server / +1,176 B client).
overclaim_risk: Per-request bytes assumed, not captured from a real attack; reuse of challenge cookies lowers CAPTCHA/PoW cost further.
underclaim_risk: Attackers on free botnet egress (compromised devices) pay near zero proxy cost; the sheet is a rented-pool cost.

title: Defender CPU per stage on a $5 VPS, marked measured vs assumed
summary: $5/mo fully utilised vCPU = $1.9e-6 per CPU-second. Stage costs on the reference core (i9-14900HX), scaled /0.5 for a $5 shared vCPU (cpu_scale=0.5 is an E assumption): TLS1.3 full handshake 424 us ref (rustls 0.23.37, 2,357 hs/s/core; InfoQ 2026-09; grade C, suite unstated) => 848 us on VPS; resumed 138 us ref (7,249/s/core) => 276 us; hybrid ML-KEM adds ~21% server CPU (Red Sift/OpenSSL, C). Own measurement: GCRA keyed std HashMap 18 ns @1k keys, 88 ns @65k keys, global GCRA 1.2 ns (D). r2 measured: wasmtime component fresh store+instantiate p50 20.3 us (B). Assumed (E): parse 10 us, classify 1 us, 429 write 8 us, challenge issue 150 us, verify 50 us (measured Anubis verify ceiling ~11.5k proofs/s => ~87 us under 64-way contention, C). Consequence: defender dollars per request are ~1e-9 (a rejected request after full TLS costs ~1.7e-9 USD); the binding constraint is capacity: one vCPU saturates at ~1,131 req/s of 429-after-TLS (941/s with hybrid ML-KEM) and ~32 req/s of cost-100 handler work.
specifics: Own microbench: 07-work/gcra_bench.rs (std only, rustc -O, taskset core 2, 2026-10-25, binary deleted); numbers_checked in the raw JSON.
overclaim_risk: TLS number is a laptop core scaled by an assumption; ECDSA vs RSA cert, session-ticket mode and kernel costs not captured. Keyed-store timing used SipHash (pessimistic vs FxHash/DashMap).
underclaim_risk: Reject-path CPU is dominated by TLS, not by any limiter stage (limiter work is <0.1 us vs 424 us): limiter micro-optimisation is worthless; pre-TLS filtering is what moves capacity.

title: Negative: naive key-eviction under key churn costs 3.5 us per check (40x the lookup)
summary: Single-thread microbench with a 65,536-entry bounded GCRA store: 1k distinct keys 18.2 ns/check, 65k keys 87.8 ns, 1M churn keys (every new key forces an eviction implemented as keys().next()+remove) 3,509 ns. The O(n) scan is an artefact of my eviction rule, but it demonstrates that a K key-churn attacker (r2 swarm actor K) turns eviction into the hot path unless eviction is O(1) amortised (generation sweep / CLOCK / TAT-expiry bucket).
overclaim_risk: Implementation-specific; governor's retain_recent()+shrink_to_fit sweep was not benchmarked.

title: Measured PoW asymmetry: native SHA-256 62-89 MH/s vs in-browser ~150 kH/s (430-860x)
summary: pow-buster / 'Proof of Mutex' (Ryzen 9 7950X, 2025-09-06): Anubis SHA-256 single-block, native single thread 62.19 MH/s (SHA-NI) to 85.75-89.16 MH/s (AVX-512), Chromium SIMD128 14.74 MH/s, in-browser Anubis solver ~100-200 kH/s (Firefox ~20% of Chromium), multi-thread native 1.465-1.485 GH/s vs vendor solver ~650 kH/s. Corrects r2 abuse-pow-economics-calc, which used 2.3 MH/s from an e2-micro: a modern native solver does a d4 (16-bit) challenge in ~1 ms and d6 (24-bit) in ~0.27 s on one core, i.e. ~$1e-9 per solve. A human browser at 150 kH/s needs 0.44 s for 16 bits, 1.7 s for 18 bits and 112 s for 24 bits (phones slower; the sim assumes 5x, E). Anubis v1.28.0 (2026-10-08) .. v1.28.2 (2026-10-23) adds opt-in WASM PoW (Argon2id, HashX, SHA-256; difficulty counts leading bits: Fast/Moderate/Strong = 8/16/24 bits SHA-256, 7/15/20 HashX, 2/4/6 Argon2id), disabled by default, no published performance numbers; memory-hard variants are the only change that could alter the asymmetry and are unmeasured here.
specifics: Author-run benchmarks on one CPU; vendor figure 650 kH/s disagrees with the 150 kH/s browser figure by 4x (WASM optimisation/throttling).
overclaim_risk: Do not read this as 'PoW is useless': it is a speed bump plus a way to force a client to run JS/WASM; but no difficulty a phone tolerates changes attacker cost.
underclaim_risk: Argon2id/HashX WASM modes (v1.28) were not measured; they may restore some asymmetry.

title: 2026 swarm shape: 1.2M IPs, ~1 request per 9 s per IP (DataDome campaign, mid-April 2026, secondary reports)
summary: Secondary reports (Clubic, Rankiteo, CyberSecurityNews/VPNCentral) of a DataDome-detected L7 campaign: 2.45B malicious requests in ~5 h (avg ~136k rps, peak 205,344 rps), 1.2M unique IPs, 16,402 ASNs, ~1 request per 9 s per IP, waves with pauses. The sim's per-IP rate 0.1 req/s (10k IPs => 1,000 rps) reproduces the per-IP shape, scaled to what a 1 vCPU box could even see. Cloudflare's 25th DDoS report (H1 2026): HTTP DDoS requests 12.75T (Q1) -> 16.89T (Q2); >1 Tbps attacks 130 -> 805 Q1->Q2 (context). Imperva 2024: ~25% of bad-bot traffic from residential ISPs (secondary).
specifics: No DataDome primary page found; ASN count from one aggregator.
overclaim_risk: Vendor-reported; the target platform was a large UGC site, not a small origin.

title: Netflix concurrency-limits library defaults do not fit a 1 vCPU box (Gradient2 min=20, initial=20, queue const 4)
summary: Source read 2026-10-25: Gradient2Limit builder initialLimit=20, minLimit=20, maxConcurrency=200, smoothing 0.2, rttTolerance 1.5, longWindow 600, queueSize = constant 4 (not sqrt), app-limited guard inflight < limit/2, longRtt*0.95 when long/short > 2. VegasLimit initial 20, max 1000, alpha=3*log10(L), beta=6*log10(L), smoothing 1.0, probe multiplier 30. The r2 spec (start 16, min 4, max 64) was a deviation; in the sim, raising Lmin to 20 with an unprotected pipeline raised human p99 455 -> 730 ms (CAND mixed), and fixed L=64 gave 2.7 s vs 197 ms at L=4. Once S3 aggregate budgets cap admitted work, the limiter never binds (see r3e07-limiter-dormant).
specifics: Code facts A; sim consequences D.

title: NEGATIVE: the r2 L5 default pipeline collapses under a 10k-IP solver swarm; no single-parameter change rescues it
summary: Simulation (heapq DES, 120 s, 3-10 seeds; 200 humans, 10 verified agents, 10k-IP solver swarm at 1,000 rps cost-100 + heavy hitter 300 rps): r2 defaults give human failure 99.1% (max 99.4% over seeds 1-10), human server-side p99 3,793 ms vs 46.8 ms unloaded, verified-agent success 59.7%. In 178 single-parameter sweep points (~45 parameters x 3 seeds: s1_rate, anon/sess budgets, L0/Lmin/Lmax, qmax, CoDel, ladder levels, PoW bits, cpu_scale, conn caps, shares) human FP stays 98-100% for all except: exp_frac<1 (26%), fresh_class on (47%), ladder off / max_level 0 (47%), ladder_cost_aware (81%), tls_full_cap 0.2 (87%), anon_burst=30 (16%, because anon burst < cost-100 makes the deep path unreachable without a session). Root causes: (1) PoW-minted cookies land in the same 'session' class as returning humans, so the swarm owns that queue (I3 isolation violated); (2) no concurrency cap on the expensive tier (cost-100 = 30 ms) so 4-8 swarm requests starve everything; (3) per-identity budgets irrelevant because each of 10k identities stays under its own budget. Other scenarios on r2 defaults (10 seeds): naive swarm 22.8% FP (new humans 70.9%), browser swarm 34.2%, aged-cookie swarm 92.6%, cheap flood (cost 5) 75.5%, 1k-IP datacenter swarm 84.8%; heavy single IP only 1.4% (per-IP limit works against one IP).
specifics: Files: 07-work/panel_r2.jsonl (10 seeds x 10 scenarios), sweeps_r2_mixed.jsonl (178 sweep points x 3 seeds). Sim: /home/patrickd/aegis/research/state/raw/round-003/07-work/swarm_sim.py
overclaim_risk: One simulator; PS CPU, fixed service times and my cookie-class semantics are modelling choices; magnitude (99%) is model-dependent but the mechanism list is structural.
underclaim_risk: Not a claim that r2's ordering is wrong: S0/S1 ordering is sound; the failure is class design and missing aggregate caps.

title: NEGATIVE: per-IP-only limiting collapses where each IP sends <=0.1 req/s; per-identity budgets do not bind either
summary: Config S0+S1 only (per-/32 GCRA, no concurrency control) vs swarm: at 0.01 req/s/IP (100 rps total) human FP 74%, at 0.1 req/s/IP 98%, human p99 63 s, verified agents 2% success; swarm admitted 2,047 units/s (the whole CPU). Heavy single IP: FP 0%, attacker 5 ok/s (per-IP limiter works). With full pipeline, session budgets 150-3,000 units/min and burst 300-3,000 have zero effect on the mixed scenario because 10k IPs x 0.1 req/s x 100 units = 10 units/s per identity = exactly one session budget (600/min). Attacker spend to hold this up on mid-price proxies: ~$115-133/hour at 1,000 rps (7.4 KB/attempt incl. TLS); at 1 req/IP/9 s the sustained cost scales linearly (DataDome-shape 136k rps => ~$14k/hour at $4/GB and 7.4 KB/attempt, derived and unverified).

title: NEGATIVE: full TLS handshakes cap a 1 vCPU box at ~1.1k connections/s; rejects after TLS cannot protect humans
summary: At cpu_scale 0.5 (E) a swarm of 1,000 new-connection rps consumes 85% of the CPU in handshakes alone; the sim's 5 ms accept windows then drop arrivals at random, so human FP has a floor equal to the drop fraction (CAND base 13.8%, fixed to 8.1% by reserving window budget for resumed/keep-alive). Mitigation tested: tls_full_cap = share of the CPU window usable by FULL handshakes: 1.0 -> human FP 7.9%/p99 470 ms; 0.8 -> 7.5%; 0.6 -> 0.9%/170 ms; 0.4 -> 0.9%/85 ms; 0.2 -> 0.8%/59 ms (TUNED base). Cost: new visitors lose handshakes first (new-visitor FP 3%). CPU sensitivity (TUNED): cpu_scale 0.25..2.0 keeps FP 0.8-1.5%. Hybrid X25519MLKEM768 adds ~21% server handshake CPU (Red Sift, OpenSSL) and ~1.1 KB each way: capacity 1,131 -> 941 rps. A CPU-keyed challenge trigger is actively harmful: challenges cannot cheapen handshakes, so the ladder climbed to the 24-bit rung and human FP went 12% -> 23% (CAND).
overclaim_risk: The fix depends on the server being able to tell a resumable client before spending crypto (PSK/ticket identity is visible in ClientHello); not implemented in any stack I verified.
underclaim_risk: A kernel/XDP pre-TLS filter or an upstream CDN/SYN-proxy would remove this floor entirely; not simulated.

title: NEGATIVE: the 24-bit PoW rung excludes humans and the load-keyed ladder had no measurable effect once class budgets existed
summary: Human cost at measured browser speed 150 kH/s: 16 bit 0.44 s, 18 bit 1.7 s, 20 bit 7 s, 24 bit 112 s (phones 5x, E). CAND mixed sweep: top-rung bits 16/18 -> human FP 9-10%, 20/22 -> 15%, 24 -> 23% (new visitors 58%). Attacker expensive successes were flat at 6.0-6.2/s across 16-24 bits (native solver 62 MH/s: 24 bits = 0.27 s), so PoW difficulty did not change attacker admission at all. On the TUNED pipeline the ladder (on/off, max_level 0-3, trigger thresholds, bits) changed nothing: the stress signal (anon-queue sojourn >5 ms for 100 ms) never fired because S3 aggregate budgets and the tier cap keep queues short. The only PoW that mattered was the step-up challenge for anonymous cost>=100 requests at ANY load (stepup_cost 100 vs none: human FP 2.7% -> 1.1%, humans pay one 16-bit solve = 0.44 s desktop / ~2.2 s phone).
overclaim_risk: Ladder may matter in scenarios not modelled (unknown-cost endpoints, cache-miss storms); it is demoted to E-grade backstop, not removed.

title: NEGATIVE: age-based session promotion is bypassed by a slow swarm; needs an established-class expensive aggregate
summary: Fresh-session class (cookie younger than 60 s) isolates PoW-minted cookies from humans (human FP 3.0% without the class vs 0.9% with it in the TUNED mixed scenario; fresh_age 10 s -> 2.9% and attacker 634 units/s; 60-300 s equivalent). But a swarm at 0.01-0.03 req/s/IP (10k IPs = 100-300 rps, cookie reused up to 100 times) waits out the age and enters the established class: with only a fresh/anon aggregate (300 units/s), single-seed trials showed attacker admitted 1,213-1,359 units/s; adding a separate established-class expensive aggregate (400 units/s) cut it to 436-502 units/s (single seed) and to 510 units/s worst-of-10 seeds in the aged_swarm panel (human FP 2.5% mean, 3.7% max). Promotion must be behaviour- and cost-based, not age-only.
specifics: Files: panel_tuned2.jsonl (aged_swarm), try runs in session log.
overclaim_risk: Attacker model keeps one cookie per IP and reuses it; a smarter farmer could spread requests.

title: NEGATIVE: a pre-auth per-IP bucket of 5 req/s burst 20 throttles verified agents that legitimately send 5 req/s
summary: Verified agents (10, Poisson 5 req/s each, one IP each) hit the r2 S1 default (5 req/s, burst 20): 3% 429 in baseline; s1_rate 1 -> 20% success, 2 -> 40%, >=5 -> 99.8-100% (TUNED). CG-NAT: 20 humans behind one IP at 4 req/s total are at 80% of the S1 limit; at 50 humans (flash crowd) NAT-human FP 21% (max 26%) even at s1_rate 10 / anon_upm 600, 80% on r2 defaults. Anonymous NAT users never get a cookie at level 0, so only a soft session cookie or Privacy-Pass-style token can lift them out of the per-IP bucket.

title: Adaptive concurrency limiter (Gradient2/Vegas) had no measurable effect after S3 aggregate caps; fixed L=4-8 is as good
summary: TUNED mixed sweeps: algo gradient2 vs vegas, L0 4/8/16/32, Lmin 1-20, Lmax 8-200, fixed L 2-64, g_tol 1.1-3, g_queue 1-16: human FP 0.9% and p99 82-85 ms throughout, plausibly because admitted work is capped by S3 below ~50% CPU and inflight stays under the app-limited guard (inflight < L/2); not instrumented. In the unprotected CAND base, fixed L=4 gave p99 197 ms vs 2,702 ms at L=64, and adaptive Gradient2 from L0=16 stayed near 15.9 (did not beat fixed L=8 in the TUNED1 base: 336 ms vs 410 ms). Interpretation: on 1 vCPU with PS CPU and 0.5x io, RTT grows linearly with L and the gradient signal is weak; the limiter is a backstop, not the primary defence.
overclaim_risk: Model has no cache/GC/IO variance that would make RTT noisy and the gradient informative.
underclaim_risk: Do not delete S5: unknown-cost overload is not in the scenario set.

title: L5: deterministic discrete-event simulator of S0-S6 (python stdlib, heapq) - code path, model and CI invocation
summary: Path: /home/patrickd/aegis/research/state/raw/round-003/07-work/swarm_sim.py (+ exp.py, sweep1.py, sweep2.py, panel.py, cost_model.py, gcra_bench.rs; data *.jsonl, tuned.json). Run: `python3 -I swarm_sim.py quick`; sweeps via `python3 -I sweep1.py {R2|TUNED|CAND} mixed out.jsonl`; 10-seed acceptance via `python3 -I panel.py tuned.json out.jsonl` (seeds 1..10; 120 s virtual, 20 s warm-up; ~1-2 s CPU per run). Model: Poisson generators (humans 200 @0.2 req/s with 20 behind one CG-NAT IP, 5% no-JS accessible, 30% new; 10 verified agents @5 req/s; swarm N IPs @r req/s with IP lifetime L requests, kinds naive/solver/browser; heavy hitter ignoring 429); PS CPU via virtual-time heap with 5 ms accept windows stealing speed and dropping arrivals; S0 conn caps, S1 GCRA per /32 with LRU-bounded store + /24 aggregate, S3 per-identity cost GCRA (verified/session/fresh/anon), S4 cookie-minting challenge ladder (meta-refresh, 16/24-bit PoW) with measured solve rates, S5 4 identity classes x {cheap, expensive} queues, share-weighted drain, per-queue CoDel, anon LIFO, Gradient2/Vegas per Netflix source, S6 handler = cpu (0.2/1/4/30 ms for cost 1/5/20/100) + 0.5x io. Attacker $ accounted per byte ($4/GB default) and per solve. Findings from ~180 sweep points x 3 seeds per base on 4 bases, structural sweeps, plus 10-seed panels; total ~3,400 runs. Seed is recorded in every output record. Deterministic: same seed -> identical JSON.
specifics: Calibration gaps: service times from r2 spec (E), cpu_scale 0.5 (E), human/phone PoW rates (C/E), no real-hardware validation, no replay of SourceHut/GNOME logs. 'Pure python, <100 MB RSS; ran at nice 19 outside heavy.sh because sibling cargo builds held the lock'.
overclaim_risk: Passing the sim is necessary not sufficient; real-hardware load test (BENCH_PLAN) must repeat the 10-seed panel.
underclaim_risk: A calibrated DES surfaced six structural failure modes that a survey missed; value is in the failure list, not in absolute numbers.

title: L5: tuned default-parameter table for S0-S6 (1 vCPU / 1-2 GB), replacing the r2 E-grade proposals
summary: Format: param | r2 default -> tuned default | evidence and break point (TUNED = 3 seeds, mixed attack; grade D unless stated). S0: max_conns 2048, ip_conn_cap 32 (no effect 128-8192 / 4-128; E). NEW tls_full_cap 0.5 of each 5 ms accept window for FULL handshakes (1.0/0.8 -> FP 7.5-7.9%; 0.6 -> 0.9%; 0.2-0.4 -> 0.8-0.9%). S1: s1_rate 5 -> 10 req/s, burst 20 -> 50 (<=2 req/s: verified ok 20-40%, NAT FP 46-74%; >=5 fine); store 65,536 LRU with O(1) eviction (no effect 1k-1M here; microbench says eviction must be O(1)); /24 aggregate 50/s (no effect on residential spread). S3: anon_upm 60 -> 600 units/min, burst 120 -> 600 (NAT/new FP 1% -> <=0.5%); sess 600/1200 (no effect 150-3000: does not bind); NEW fresh_class on, fresh_age 60 s, shares (verified .30, established .40, fresh .10, anon .20) (without: FP 3.0%); NEW stepup_cost 100 units (anonymous cost>=100 gets 16-bit PoW at any load: FP 2.7% -> 1.1%); NEW agg_exp_units_s 300 (fresh+anon expensive-tier aggregate GCRA, burst 2 s, charged at S5 admission; attacker admitted units ~= setting +40: 100->141, 300->341, 600->640, 1200->1238) and agg_exp_est_units_s 400 (established; needed against aged cookies); exp_cost 20, exp_frac 0.25 (redundant once aggregates set; keep as depth). S4: ladder trigger = anon-queue sojourn only (drop CPU trigger: FP 23% -> 12% on CAND), lvl_up_every 1 -> 5 s, PoW bits {rung2 16, rung3 18} instead of {16, 24} (24-bit = 112 s in browser); accessible lane required (no-JS user FP 33% without vs 10% with, CAND). S5: L0 16 -> 8, Lmin 4, Lmax 32 (Netflix lib defaults 20/20/200 are wrong for 1 vCPU), algo gradient2 (tolerance 1.5, queue const 4, window 0.5 s) - dormant, qmax 32 (R2 base: qmax 128 -> p99 20.8 s, 512 -> 51.6 s), CoDel target 20 ms for cheap queues and 250 ms for the expensive queue (0.02 -> FP 5.2% vs 0.9%), interval 100 ms, anon LIFO on (no effect). S6: hard deadline and post-hoc debit untested in the sim. cpu_scale sensitivity: 0.25..2.0 -> FP 0.8-1.5%, attacker units 294-473/s.
specifics: Evidence files: sweeps_tuned2_mixed.jsonl (187 points), sweeps_cand_mixed.jsonl, sweeps_r2_mixed.jsonl, tuned.json is the machine-readable table. Every number is a simulator output, not a measurement of a real server.
overclaim_risk: Parameters tuned on one scenario family (solver swarm + heavy hitter + humans); overfit risk to that family, mitigated by the 10-scenario panel but not by out-of-model validation.
underclaim_risk: Declining to publish numbers would leave implementers with the r2 defaults that fail 99% in the sim.

title: L5: swarm acceptance criteria with pass/fail numbers (10 seeds x 10 scenarios), r2 defaults vs tuned vs per-IP-only
summary: Criteria (C) and measured results (mean/worst over seeds 1-10, mixed scenario unless noted): C1 human failure <= 2% (r2 99.1% FAIL; per-IP-only 97.8% FAIL; TUNED 0.9%/max 1.3% PASS). C2 human server-side p99 <= 3x unloaded (46.8 ms => 140 ms) (r2 3,793 ms FAIL; per-IP 57.7 s FAIL; TUNED 81.6/max 92.4 ms PASS). C3 verified agents >= 99% (r2 59.7% FAIL; per-IP 2.1% FAIL; TUNED 100% PASS). C4 attacker admitted expensive units/s <= 20% of capacity = 667 (3,333 units/s = 1 vCPU / 30 ms x 100) (r2 751-785 FAIL; per-IP 2,062 FAIL; TUNED 366 max, aged swarm 510, dc swarm 369 PASS). C5 CG-NAT and no-JS humans FP <= 5% under attack (TUNED mixed 1.0%/3.2% and 1.4%/4.5% PASS; flash-crowd of 50 NAT users 21%/26% FAIL - known gap). C6 cheap flood (cost 5, 391 admitted req/s): human FP <= 2% (TUNED 0.0% PASS; r2 75.5% FAIL); p99 177/max 215 ms. C7 aged-cookie swarm: FP <= 5%, units <= 667 (TUNED 2.5%/max 3.7% and 510 PASS; r2 92.6% FAIL). C8 single heavy hitter 300 rps (structural sweep to 3,000 rps: FP 0.0%): FP <= 1% and attacker <= 1 ok_exp/s (TUNED 0.0% and 0.5/s PASS; r2 1.4% FAIL by margin). C9 baseline humans only: FP <= 1% (TUNED 0.0%; r2 1.3% FAIL on NAT 9.9%/22.7% max - anon bucket). C10 accept-window overhead utilisation (TLS/limiter/challenge stages; handler PS work not separately reported) <= 85% (TUNED 0.27-0.45 PASS; r2 0.75-0.78 under swarm). C11 no-fail-open and key-churn memory bound: NOT tested in the sim (spike). C12 PoW-solved share: with solver swarm, attacker-minted sessions are 100% of fresh-class admits; layer declared ineffective per r2 criterion (9) and carried by budgets - CONFIRMED. Attacker economics reported alongside (not a pass criterion): $124/hour to sustain 1,000 rps (mid proxies), $0.0102 per successful expensive request (99% of attempts rejected), r2 base $0.005.
specifics: Files: panel_tuned2.jsonl, panel_r2.jsonl, panel_perip.jsonl. Gate: fixed seeds 1..10 in CI, nightly random seeds, fail if any worst-seed value breaches.
overclaim_risk: Thresholds are mine (r2 proposed similar); 667 units/s derived from the service-time model.
underclaim_risk: Worst-seed values reported to avoid mean-hiding.

title: L5: attacker/defender cost model sheet (machine-readable) with dated prices and provenance marks
summary: cost_model.json (script cost_model.py): sections sources, attacker_per_1M_requests_usd (4 classes x 3 proxy price points x admitted/rejected), managed_per_1M_pages_usd, attacker_llm_per_1M_usd (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus 5.5), defender_stage_cost (each stage: us on ref core, us on $5 VPS at scale 0.5, USD per 1M, provenance grade B/C/D/E), usd_per_cpu_second (1.9e-6), saturate_one_vcpu: 429-after-TLS 1,131 rps => attacker $60/$121/$181 per hour at $2/$4/$6 per GB; challenge-after-TLS 855 rps => $46-137/h; cost-100 handler 32 rps => $1.7-5.2/h (!); hybrid ML-KEM 941 rps => $66-197/h. Reading: the cheapest way to take down an unprotected cost-100 endpoint is $2-5/hour, ~30x cheaper than saturating TLS; making expensive endpoints cheap or capped moves the attacker to the $60-200/hour TLS floor. Re-run annually: prices stale by 2027-Q1.

title: L5: additional spec invariants I8-I10 implied by the simulation (extends abuse-L5-budget-invariants)
summary: I8 (expensive-tier aggregate): for any window W, sum of admitted cost units with cost >= C_exp from identities in {fresh, anon} <= A_f*W + burst, and from {established} <= A_e*W + burst, regardless of identity count (defaults A_f=300, A_e=400 units/s, burst = 2 s).
